summary: Vincent Eltschinger specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Fribourg, Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, and Vienna. He held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, IKGA, and became a directeur d’études at EPHE around 2015.

Vincent Goossaert works in sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology, having studied under Kristofer Schipper. He served at CNRS (around 1998–2012), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (2007), and became Professor of Daoist History at EPHE around 2012.

Vincent Lefèvre specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Bruno Dagens, and has served as a curator at the Musée Guimet.

Vincent Tournier specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at EPHE, Leiden, and under Seishi Karashima and Cristina Scherrer-Schaub. His appointments include EFEO (attested 2021) and positions attested in 2026 at the University of Tokyo and Göttingen Academy.
Vincenzo Vergiani works in Indology and linguistics, having studied under teacher Raffaele Torella. Around 2009, he became Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge.

Indologist Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar studied at St. Xavier's, St John's, Edinburgh, and Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, Hermann Jacobi, and Moriz Winternitz. He served at the Archaeological Survey of India (1915–1919) and Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute from 1925.

Vishvanath Narayan Mandlik was an Indologist and historian who studied at Elphinstone College under Ramachandra Balkrishna. He served as Vice-President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1878) and as an examiner at the University of Mumbai.

Vishwa Nath Pathak was an Indologist and historian who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts, including professor, at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (attested 1978 and 1987).

Vishwanath Prasad Varma worked in philosophy, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied under Dhirendra Mohan Datta, Ganga Nath Bhattacharya, doctoral supervisor Kali Kinkar Datta, and Joachim Wach (1950).

Indologist Vishwanathan Venkatachalam studied at Madras, Nagpur, and Vikram Universities. His main posts included Director of Scindia Oriental Institute (around 1972–1985) and Vice-Chancellor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1986–1989, 1992–1995) and Kameshwar Singh Darbhanga Sanskrit University (1996–1998).
Vitus Angermeier works in Indology, having studied under Karin Preisendanz, Chlodwig H. Werba, and Roque Mesquita. He holds an appointment as a lecturer at the University of Vienna (attested 2026).

Vladimir Balabushevich was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Head of the Indian Department at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (attested 1970 and 1990).

Vladimir Kalyanov was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Institute for Philosophy, Literature and History in Leningrad and under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. He worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts from around 1938 to 2001.

Vladimir Minorsky worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history. He studied at Moscow Imperial University and the Lazarev Institute, later holding posts at INALCO (around 1923–1932) and SOAS University of London (around 1932–1944).

Vladimir Tikhonov specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and religious studies. Educated at Saint Petersburg State, Korea, and Moscow State universities, he taught at Kyung Hee University before becoming Associate Professor (2000) and Professor (2006) at the University of Oslo.

Tibetologist Volker Caumanns studied at the Universities of Hamburg and Munich under David P. Jackson and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He held posts at Munich (2006–2012) and LIRI (2012–2015), with later appointments at Bern, Hamburg, and Leipzig.

Volker Grabowsky specializes in history and Southeast Asian studies. Educated at Kiel and Chiang Mai, he held posts at Passau, Münster, and the National University of Laos, before becoming Chair of Thai Studies at the University of Hamburg in 2009.

Volker Zotz is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Vienna and under Anagarika Govinda, later teaching at Vienna, Otani, Ryukoku, Saarland, and Luxembourg universities.
W. F. Jayasuriya was a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Rerukane Ariyaratne, H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, and M. U. Sri Kaveeswara.

W. H. R. Rivers studied medicine at the University of London. He held posts at several hospitals, taught at Cambridge from 1893, became a Fellow of St John's College in 1902, and served as Anthropological Society of London president (around 1921–1922).
